bills.title: Homeowners Premium Tax Reduction Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9978 would create or expand a tax deduction or credit for homeowners' insurance premiums, directly implicating IRS authority under Treasury and the Joint Committee on Taxation's revenue scoring process. Treasury's Office of Tax Policy must assess the revenue cost, potential for abuse or misuse of the benefit, and any administrative burden the new provision places on IRS for implementation and compliance.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to improve the process for providing refunds to taxpayers.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5142 directly amends the Internal Revenue Code, placing implementation responsibility on IRS and oversight authority with Treasury's Office of Tax Policy. Changes to the refund process carry significant fiscal risk, including potential increases in improper payments and cash-flow timing effects on the federal budget.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to eliminate installment agreement fees for certain individuals.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5144 directly affects IRS tax administration under Treasury's jurisdiction by amending IRC installment agreement provisions, which are administered by IRS's Small Business/Self-Employed and Wage and Investment divisions. The fee elimination would reduce user-fee revenue currently authorized under 31 U.S.C. 9701 and require IRS to update its installment agreement processing systems and cost-recovery accounting, creating both a budget impact and an operational implementation burden.

bills.title: ABLE MATCH (Making Able a Tool to Combat Hardship) Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9801 would create a federal matching contribution for ABLE account deposits made by low-income eligible individuals, directly implicating IRS authority over tax-advantaged savings accounts under IRC Section 529A. Treasury and IRS would bear responsibility for designing and administering the matching mechanism, including income verification, contribution limits, and coordination with existing means-tested benefit rules.

bills.title: A bill to amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to impose limitations on high-income taxpayers with large retirement account balances.
bills.status: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
bills.nexus: S. 5040 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy by amending the Internal Revenue Code to cap or reduce tax-preferred retirement accumulations for high-income individuals. Treasury faces significant implementation risk, including rulemaking requirements to define thresholds, coordinate with DOL on ERISA-governed plans, and potential revenue estimation disputes with JCT.

bills.title: To amend the Internal Revenue Code of 1986 to impose limitations on high-income taxpayers with large retirement account balances.
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9813 directly implicates IRS and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy because it would amend the Internal Revenue Code to cap tax-advantaged retirement account balances for high-income earners, requiring new regulatory definitions and contribution rules. Implementation risk centers on IRS's capacity to build the data infrastructure needed to monitor aggregate account balances across custodians and issue guidance on required minimum distributions or excess-balance excise taxes.

bills.title: Putting Patients First by Strengthening Provider Accountability in FECA Act
bills.status: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.
bills.nexus: H.R. 8823 amends the Federal Employees' Compensation Act, which is administered by the Department of Labor, not Treasury, and its provider accountability provisions do not触及 Treasury's tax, revenue, financial stability, or fiscal authorities. Treasury has no identified programmatic or implementation equities in this legislation.

bills.title: Tariff Refund Act of 2026
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9768 directly implicates Treasury's Office of Tax Policy and the U.S. Customs Revenue function administered through CBP under Treasury's historical authority, as tariff refund mechanisms affect customs duty collections that flow to the General Fund. The implementation risk centers on the potential administrative burden of processing retroactive refund claims and the revenue scoring implications that Treasury and OMB would need to model for the Ways and Means markup.

bills.title: Disclosure of Tax Havens and Offshoring Act
bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Financial Services.
bills.nexus: H.R. 9761 would require public country-by-country reporting of corporate tax and financial data, directly implicating IRS authority under the Internal Revenue Code and Treasury's Office of Tax Policy, which oversees international tax rules and OECD/BEPS alignment. The implementation risk centers on Treasury coordinating disclosure standards with SEC reporting requirements while managing potential competitive harm to U.S. multinationals and ensuring consistency with existing OECD Pillar Two frameworks.

bills.status: Referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.
